resources.string: One-tap lock from your home screen
Ghost mode keeps TapLock invisible to UPI and banking apps. Accessibility is only enabled for a split second when you lock.
1. Connect your phone to a PC with USB debugging\n2. Run both commands below\n3. Re-open TapLock and turn off developer options
Run both commands below. On some devices, also enable the USB debugging security toggle in Developer options first.
UPI apps won\u2019t see TapLock in accessibility. Fingerprint and face unlock work normally after locking.
TapLock stays enabled in Accessibility settings. Some UPI and banking apps may refuse to run until you disable it.
Locks the screen when you tap the TapLock home screen widget. Does not read screen content.
Answers about setup, widgets, UPI apps, and privacy
TapLock briefly enables its accessibility service only while locking (~700 ms), then removes itself. UPI apps never see it in your accessibility list.
Long-press your home screen \u2192 Widgets \u2192 TapLock \u2192 drag it on. On some phones you can also long-press the TapLock app icon and choose Add widgets.
Re-run the two setup commands from a PC, then open TapLock again. Turn developer options back on first if you disabled them.
If you can\u2019t run ADB commands, enable TapLock manually in Accessibility settings. Banking apps may block while it stays on.
No internet, no analytics, no screen reading. TapLock only performs the system lock action.
1. Long-press an empty area on your home screen\n2. Tap Widgets\n3. Find TapLock and drag it to your home screen
On some phones (Samsung, Xiaomi, OnePlus, and others), you can also long-press the TapLock app icon on your home screen or app drawer and choose Add widgets or Widgets.
Tap the widget any time to lock your phone with the shackle animation.
